label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Monday 30 Nov, Embakasi: casuals' pay, what to say and what to do if they won't load

Brian,

This is for you to read on Sunday. Short version first, detail underneath.

THE SHORT VERSION

- Friday's pay failed because of our file. It is nothing the guys did, and all 212 were affected.
- The money will be on their phones by 11am Monday, by M-Pesa. That is the only time you give anyone.
- Everyone on the list gets an extra KES 500 for lunch and fare in the same payment. The M-Pesa charges are ours and nobody is deducted.
- You apologise in person, on behalf of management. Njeri asked for that and she's right.
- Speak to Ouma privately before you speak to the group.
- No threats about contracts or future shifts, whatever happens with the trucks.
- WhatsApp me before I board if anything changes. I'm up from 4:30 and the flight is 7:05.

WHAT HAPPENED ON FRIDAY

Finance sent the casuals' pay file to the bank as usual. The bank upgraded its platform on Wednesday 25th and now wants a new file template. Ours was still in the old format, so the whole file was rejected and nobody was paid.

The rejection notice went to an old finance mailbox. Kevin only saw it after 5pm, when the bank's cut-off had passed. He has said plainly that this one is on finance.

On Saturday morning Njeri approved skipping the bank and paying everyone by M-Pesa instead.

Tell it to them that simply: the bank changed its format, our file was rejected, and we found out too late on Friday to fix it the same day. Don't lean on the bank. They made the change but we are the ones who didn't catch it. That is the whole reason Friday failed, and if people start guessing at other reasons, bring them back to it.

WHEN THE MONEY LANDS

By 11am Monday. That is Kevin's realistic time. He will not promise earlier, so neither do we.

You remember Mombasa in 2024. The supervisor told the casuals "by lunch", the money came at 4pm and half the shift sat down. Joseph says the guys are already reminding each other that last time management said "tomorrow" for three days. So give one time and say it the same way every time you're asked. Don't say "hopefully earlier" or "any time now".

If Kevin tells you anything that moves 11, tell the guys yourself, straight away, before they work it out. And tell me if I'm still on the ground.

The exception is 14 people. Peninah confirmed 198 numbers and could not reach 14, mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake. She has the list and will be at Embakasi from 7:30 with a printout so they can give her the right numbers face to face.

Until she has a correct number, their money has nowhere to go, so don't give those 14 the 11am. Tell them they see Peninah first thing and are paid once their number is confirmed. Ask her for a time for them once she has spoken to Kevin. When she arrives, get Joseph to help her find them fast.

WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE

- Full pay for the fortnight, by M-Pesa, on their phones by 11am.
- KES 500 each on top for lunch and fare, in the same payment, for every casual on the affected list.
- No M-Pesa charges deducted from anyone.
- Peninah on site from 7:30. She will have her laptop and will print a payslip for anyone who wants to check their amount.
- Nobody loses anything for being angry about this. They have a right to be.
- Anything they want to raise formally goes through Joseph to me and HR answers within 48 hours. I'll do that from Kampala.

WHAT YOU MUSTN'T PROMISE

- Any time earlier than 11am, even to one person, even quietly. It will be round the yard in five minutes.
- Cash in hand on the day. There isn't any arranged.
- Anything beyond the 500. If someone asks about rent on the 1st or other compensation, say you'll take it to me and Njeri, and then do it. Don't agree to anything on the spot.
- That it will never happen again. They've heard that before. Say what went wrong and that finance is fixing it, and leave it there.

HOW TO GO IN

This is our mess, not theirs. The guys did the work and did nothing wrong, so don't go in defensive and don't argue about tone. If someone shouts, let him finish.

You'll be there at 5:30 and the shift comes in at 6. Find Joseph first and get the temperature from him. He has been trying to calm them since Saturday and he'll know who is leading and who is just following.

Then find Ouma, before the group. He is loud but he is not a bad man. He has four kids and rent due, and he's saying what most of them are thinking.

Take him aside, just the two of you. Apologise to him directly and tell him everything you're about to tell the group: the reason, the 11am, the 500. Ask him what he needs to hear. Don't ask him to control the others for you and don't offer him anything the rest aren't getting. If he walks back to the group having heard it straight from you, half your work is done.

Then talk to the whole group. Start with the apology. Then give the reason, the time, the 500, the charges, and Peninah at 7:30. Keep it short and take questions.

IF OUMA'S GROUP WON'T LOAD THE KISUMU TRUCKS

Be honest with yourself and with them about what we're asking. The trucks have to leave by 9 to make the offloading slot at the mill and the money lands by 11. So we are asking them to load on our word, two hours before they see anything. Say that out loud. Don't dress it up.

The order I would go in:

1. Ask, don't instruct. Tell them the Kisumu trucks have to be out by 9 or we lose the slot at the mill, that the money is coming by 11 whether they load or not, and that you are asking them to load on your word. You will be standing in that yard at 11 either way, and you should say so.

2. Make it clear the pay is not tied to loading. It is for work already done and it goes to everyone on the list, including anyone who sits down. Never let it sound like "load and you'll be paid". That is the fastest way to lose them.

3. If Ouma's group still refuses, don't push them in front of everyone. Work with whoever is willing. Who loads instead and whether to call the mill about the slot are your calls as Ops, and you know better than I do how late you can leave it.

4. Nobody is sent home or struck off. Nobody is told anything about their contract or their next shift. Don't take down the names of those refusing, because it will be read as a threat even if you don't mean it as one. Our own procedure (v3, in this folder) says no one is dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day. That holds even if the trucks miss the slot.

5. The same procedure says a stoppage is handled by Ops and HR together. With me travelling, the HR half is me on the phone. That means before I board, and again once I've landed in Entebbe. So nothing about any individual gets decided on Monday. If you feel pushed towards a decision like that, it waits for me.

6. Once the money lands, go back to them, including the ones who refused. Ask if everyone has received it and send anyone who hasn't to Peninah.

If the trucks go late because of this, that is a cost of our mistake on Friday. It is not something to recover from the casuals.

REACHING ME

I'm on WhatsApp from 4:30am until I board, and again after I land. I'm in Kampala until Wednesday evening.

Message me before 7 if anything changes: Kevin's time, the mood when you arrive, or how it went with Ouma. Even "all quiet" is useful.

Achieng
